title: Great Northern Beans, Canned, Sodium Added, Drained and Rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Great Northern beans are large, light‑white beans often sold canned with added salt. After draining and rinsing they retain a tender texture and a mild nutty flavor, making them ideal for soups, stews, and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Great Northern beans belong to the legume family and are close relatives of navy beans and pinto beans.
Canned beans usually contain added sodium to enhance flavor and shelf life.
They are a rich source of plant protein and are frequently used in vegetarian diets as a meat substitute.
These beans were first cultivated in New England, USA, in the early 19th century.
Rinsing canned beans reduces their sodium content by roughly 40 %.

items.title: High in plant protein
items.content: A typical serving (about 130 g) provides roughly 12 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Beans contain about 7 g of fiber per serving, promoting healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Consuming beans helps stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Phytochemicals in beans help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned beans can be high in salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans contain oligosaccharides that can cause flatulence in sensitive people.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Check cans for dents, swelling, or leaks to avoid the risk of foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drain the liquid, rinse the beans under cold water, and add them to soups, chili, salads, or side dishes. They can also be mashed for spreads or used in vegetarian patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 4‑5 days.
